what: The unit of every published number whose KEY NAME does not already declare one.
why: 57% of this story's 942 numbers carry their unit as a key suffix (`extent_m`, `duration_s`,
`foot_pressure_kPa`). The other 403 do not, and nothing can safely bind them -- which is how
theBiomes passed 294.19 KELVIN into a Celsius table and rendered a planet as hot desert. The
key that did it was `T_surface`: Kelvin, with nothing in the name to say so.
These are DECLARED, not renamed. `g`, `R`, `M`, `T` are universal physics symbols and
`g_m_s2` is uglier without being clearer; renaming would also break every child that reads a
parent key by name. Declaring keeps one source of truth for the VALUE and puts the unit
somewhere a human can audit in one pass.
ANYTHING NOT IN HERE STAYS UNDECLARED ON PURPOSE. A guessed unit is worse than a missing one:
it makes a bad bond look legal. `folding.py audit` reports what is still unread.
precedence: an explicit override; then the key's own suffix; then by_membrane; then global

notes.dK: greenhouse_K and dT_* are SPANS, not temperatures. 45 dK is 45 K of difference and also 45 degC of difference, because a span has no zero point. Bonding a span into an absolute socket gives a 45 K planet; the reverse gives a 279 K gradient. Both are misfolds and neither is visible to a dimension check.
notes.S_earth: insolation relative to Earth's -- a ratio, so dimensionless, but NOT a fraction: it can exceed 1 and does (1.0049 here).
notes.L: luminosity in watts. Ambiguous against length in other contexts, which is exactly why it is declared rather than left to be read.
notes.left_undeclared: S in theEmptying, A in theHorizon, and r/volume/hair in theZero are not confidently readable from their names and are deliberately left unread rather than guessed -- a guessed unit makes a bad bond look legal, which is worse than a missing one.
notes.half_integer: walk_run_per_sqrt_leg and swing_period_per_sqrt_leg are a planet's Froude COEFFICIENTS -- a speed per root-length and a period per root-length. Their dimensions are L^0.5 T^-1 and L^-0.5 T. The units table now carries fractional exponents rather than leaving the two most-published unread keys in the tree unread for a formatting reason.
notes.case: `dynamic_pressure_pa` and `P_surface_Pa` are the same unit spelled two ways. folding.py absorbs the case difference so neither hides, but the inconsistency is real and belongs to the tree, not to the reader.
notes.found_by_signatures: theGround publishes `bulk_density` with no unit, so the one membrane the vertical-stress law E2.01 was built for could not be bound to it. Surfaced by an agent trying to declare continuum mechanics -- a signature failing to dock is a real report about what a membrane publishes, not just a formatting problem.
notes.per_mass: theThrust publishes specific work and specific power -- J/kg and W/kg. Neither can be declared by a key suffix: `_per_kg` is not in SUFFIX_UNITS and any name ending `_kg` is read as a MASS, which is exactly the misfold this file exists to prevent. So they are declared here instead. folding.py's UNITS table does not yet hold J/kg or W/kg, so the audit reads the declaration and skips them rather than checking them -- a stated unit nothing can check is still better than a key silently claiming to be kilograms.
notes.theEye: Photometry enters the tree at theEye and had no representation before it: lux, candela per square metre, trolands, lumens per watt, arcminutes, arcseconds, cycles per degree, pixels per degree and steradians are all declared here. They sit in `global` rather than under a membrane because a key like `acuity_arcmin` is arcminutes no matter who publishes it -- and because `folding.py membrane <name>` calls undeclared(nums) WITHOUT the membrane, so a by_membrane declaration is invisible to the one report a chapter author actually reads.
notes.nm_reads_as_newton_metre: CAUTION, found while writing theEye: SUFFIX_UNITS is matched case-insensitively on a second pass, so ANY key ending `_nm` (nanometres) matches `_Nm` and is read as a NEWTON-METRE. That is a misfold of exactly the kind this system exists to catch, and it is invisible because both spellings look right. theEye avoids it by publishing `photopic_peak_wavelength` rather than `photopic_peak_nm`; the collision itself is still live in folding.py for anyone who types a wavelength the obvious way.
notes.hz: theStance publishes three sway frequencies in HERTZ because that is how postural sway is measured and reported everywhere, and there is no `_hz` suffix rule. They are declared here as 1/s, which is the same unit spelled the table's way, and each is ALSO published as a period in seconds so the chapter does not depend on this file to be readable.
notes.renames_owed: aHuman.dT_defended_K -> dT_defended_dK  (it is a SPAN: 33.0 degC skin minus 6.04 degC air. As an absolute Kelvin it reads 246 degrees below absolute zero.) theHuman.cadence_steps_s -> cadence_steps_per_s  (it is exactly 1/step_time_s, dimension T^-1, published under a name meaning T^1). Both are read by other membranes under the current names -- theLoad consumes cadence_steps_s -- so the rename needs its consumers moved in the same commit. Overridden now so the machine-readable truth is right today.
notes.root_blindness_2026_08_01: THE AUDIT CANNOT FAIL WHAT IT CANNOT READ. A root-first re-audit under the 2026-08-01 rules found 9 of the 34 numbers in theZero/theHorizon/theClock/theEmptying carried no readable unit -- 26% of the seed of the entire story -- including theZero.r and theZero.volume, the first two numbers there are. `folding.py audit` had been reporting 0 impossible and 0 inconsistent over them, which was true and meaningless: it reads the unit off the key name, found none, and skipped them silently. A clean audit over 74% coverage is not a clean audit. Units declared here rather than by renaming, so no consumer moves; the renames are still owed.
notes.bulk_declaration_2026_08_01: Units declared in bulk for keys whose NAME states them unambiguously (a _mm_day is mm/day, a _ratio is a ratio). Anything the name did not state was LEFT BLIND and is listed in the gate's output for reading -- a guessed unit is a misfold with a certificate on it.

overrides._note: Keys whose NAME states the wrong unit. An override is not a convenience -- it is a correction, and every entry here is a rename that is owed. Listed in renames_owed.
